$comment: Initial client JavaScript per route, gzipped kB. A ratchet: set just above what the route ships, lowered as it improves. See scripts/first-load.mjs. 2026-09-13: /, /privacy, /welcome, /prediction and /casino raised by 12-32 kB for the Watchtower error reporting SDK (@sentry/nextjs). It is loaded statically on purpose: deferring it would move the bytes out of first load but miss the hydration-time crashes that are the most valuable thing it catches. 2026-09-15: raised across the board for the Privy -> Decane migration. The Decane wallet SDK is resident in the signed-in shell, and Privy stays alongside it until the sweep retires, so the floor under every authenticated route moved. Measured, not guessed: each value is the route's actual size plus 20 kB. Before raising it, ~640 kB was taken back out of the shell by deferring the migration sheet (it mounts the whole Privy SDK) and its adapter list (which reaches into four feature barrels) behind next/dynamic - see components/layout/migration-sheet-host.tsx. These numbers come down again when the sweep is retired and Privy leaves the tree. 2026-09-22: /casino/chess/coach-lab receives a 10 kB route-specific margin because Node 24 gzip output crosses the 1900 kB default while Node 25 stays below it. 2026-09-22: the three /casino/chess/learn routes join coach-lab at 1910. They sat 1-4 kB under the 1900 default and the Last Man work moved them 5 kB WITHOUT chess importing any of it: measured against main, /casino itself and /dashboard were unchanged and the chunk count did not move, so this is shared chunks being redistributed rather than new code reaching chess. A route this close to the default crosses it on an unrelated change. 2026-09-23: /perps 1899 -> 1974 and /casino/chess/coach-lab 2206 -> 2227 after merging main (the perps desk and Last Man work); both measured against the previous commit, which built to the same sizes, plus the usual 20 kB. 2026-09-23: main's Mixpanel instrumentation (#547) adds 12-14 kB to every route; it is not one dependency that can be deferred (the SDK is already lazy; the weight is the tracking surface across ~100 call sites plus the failure-reason helper). Re-measured after merging it and set a few kB above what each route ships. 2026-09-24: /auth 1434 -> 1458 and /interests 1431 -> 1454 after merging that instrumentation here: the sign-in screen now reports auth_method_selected and login_failed, which pulls the failure-reason vocabulary into its first load (+4 kB measured), plus the usual 20 kB. 2026-09-25: the three /casino/chess/learn routes measured 2206-2209 after merging staging's Shine (#557): 3 kB of shared-chunk redistribution, as on 09-22, with chess importing none of it. Set at measured plus 20 like the rest. The same merge had put 172 kB on /auth and /interests by statically importing the migration offer into the session providers for Shine's pause; that is deferred through next/dynamic now and both routes are back where they were. 2026-09-25 (later): CI measured /casino/chess/watch at 2207 kB where this machine measures 2203, the gzip drift the 09-22 note describes, and every other chess route sits within 4 kB of the 2206 default. Chasing one kilobyte on one route moves the failure to its neighbour on the next machine, so the whole chess family carries its own entry: CI's measurement plus 20, the default untouched. 2026-09-25 (perps and prediction to production): /casino/arkjet and /casino/chicken 2206 -> 2235. Both measured 2202 on main and 2215 here, and they carry none of the restored code. The cause was isolated by building three ways: deferring the two dashboard shelves behind next/dynamic moved nothing (2215, same chunk count), and re-hiding both sections in HIDDEN_NAV_SECTIONS moved nothing either (2215). What moves it is the prediction routes being real pages again instead of the redirect stubs #517 left, which puts that feature back in the build graph and repacks the shared chunks: every signed-in route gains 13-14 kB, and these two fail only because they sat 4 kB under the default. There is no version of prediction being live that does not include its code. Set at the measured 2215 plus 20, as the 09-22 and 09-25 chess entries were. 2026-09-25 (ramping quote): the eleven chess routes with their own entry move to a fresh measured-plus-20. CI failed /casino/chess/coach-lab at 2227 against 2227 — equal on the printed figure because the report rounds with toFixed(0) while the check compares the raw float, so it was over by a fraction of a kilobyte. Measured here it is 2227.00 against a 2227 budget: zero margin. The 09-23 entry set that budget as its then-measurement plus 20, and the route has since grown into the whole margin. The rest of the family had eroded the same way, to between 3 and 7 kB, so they are re-measured together for the reason the 09-25 entry already gives: fixing one route moves the failure to its neighbour. The change that tipped it adds 0.30 kB to EVERY route (a hook, a normalizer and five locale strings in the shared graph), measured against main at 2226.69 -> 2227.00 on coach-lab and the same +0.30 on arkjet, perps and prediction/markets. Routes on the 2206 default are untouched; they have 300 kB of room. 2026-09-25 (perps budget): CI measured /perps at 1974 kB against a 1974 budget — equal on the printed figure, over by a fraction on the raw float the check compares, the toFixed(0) case the ramping-quote entry describes — where this machine measures 1971. The 09-23 entry set 1974 as its then-measurement plus 20 and the route has since grown into the whole margin, 3 kB of it gzip drift between machines. Set at CI's measurement plus 20. 2026-09-26: the sponsored-EVM registry no longer imports viem's whole chain catalogue (lib/trade/registry-chains.ts), which had ridden into the session providers and onto every signed-in route: /auth and /interests -124 kB, the casino routes -83 kB, so every route is ratcheted down to what it ships plus 8 kB of build variance. /auth and /interests are 6 kB above their previous budget on top of that drop: decane-connect-kit 2.27 (handing a session between apps, storage keyed by app) and the passkey-failed fallback on the sign-in page.
